Identical corner view of Summit House with the same tree arrangement and the same handwritten 'Beaumont Hotel 1-5-11' inscription on the mount — same print/exposure.

Local: colorized exterior postcard of Hotel Edinburgh; Cali: interior real-estate banquet scene inside the hotel — same hotel, exterior vs interior.
Local: 1968 newspaper halftone of bulldozers clearing the new fire-station site; Cali: the completed 1971 station with the LaFrance engine parked out front — same station, three years apart.
Local shows well-drilling tripod beside a dirt road; Calisphere shows a homeseekers' banquet table under sycamores — entirely different scenes.
Local is a ~18-man group portrait in front of a fire engine; Calisphere is the 628 Maple station exterior with an antique hose cart on the lawn.
Local is Laura alone on horseback in a corral (inscribed 'Laura on Pado 1911'); Calisphere shows a man on horseback beside a touring car with passengers — different scene and riders.
Local is a halftone studio portrait of a bearded man; Calisphere is a horse-drawn harvester scene in a grain field — no overlap in content.
Same 1923 bank building (matching arched entrance and pediment ornament), but local is a close-up with a mature tree and two children while Calisphere is a wide corner view with a Union Ice truck.
Same Summit House, but local (dated 1-5-11) has an empty porch and roof-mounted 'SUMMIT HOUSE.' sign, while Calisphere shows a large crowd out front with a framed porch sign — different exposure.
Local is a wide postcard view of the Triangle Service Station building; Calisphere is a close-up of three attendants posed at gas pumps — different composition and no shared architecture visible.

Identical ephemeral details — same locomotive steam-plume shape mushrooming left, same dark smoke drift from the left stack, same shed and track layout; local is just a higher-res, slightly wider scan.
Local is a color postcard of the streamline-moderne Fireside Inn in Beaumont; Calisphere is a B&W photo of the Spanish-tile San Gorgonio Inn in Banning — different buildings.
Local is a color snapshot of two firemen beside a red ladder engine outdoors; Calisphere shows the 628 Maple station facade with a hose cart — different scenes.
Local is four Stewart family members posed before a barn doorway; Calisphere is Rez Stewart on horseback beside a car — same family but entirely different photograph and setting.

Identical exposure: same 'Beaumont Garage Machine Co. Studebaker Six' placard leaning at the running board, same drapery folds, ribbon to radiator, occupant positions, background house and second car; local is a closer rephotographed print.
Same exposure of Sam's Cafe: the two pedestrians are frozen in identical mid-stride positions (one at the door, one on the sidewalk) with the same parked truck at right; only crop/contrast differ.

Local is a 1968 newspaper photo of bulldozers clearing the new fire-station site at 650 Maple; Calisphere is the completed station in 1971 with trucks in the bays — same site, wholly different photographs three years apart.
Local is an 1890-93 group portrait at a wooden clapboard schoolhouse; Calisphere shows a later Mission-style masonry school with no people — different building and exposure.
Local: ~19 men in civilian clothes posed at night before a Beaumont fire engine; Calisphere: 6 Banning firemen in turnout coats holding helmets in daylight — different department, people, and scene.
Local is a modern color close-up of the 'ERECTED 1938-39' bronze plaque; Calisphere is a B&W exterior of the City Hall building itself — related subject, entirely different photograph.
Local is a seated studio halftone portrait of a bearded man; Calisphere is a horse-drawn harvester crew in a wheat field — unrelated images.

Both show the arched-entrance stone Bank of Beaumont, but local is a close entrance view with a large eucalyptus and two children while Calisphere is a wide corner view with a lone woman — different vantage and date.

Same Summit House building, but local (dated 1-5-11) has an empty porch and bare trees while Calisphere shows a large crowd, vine-covered porch, and a Beaumont Land & Water banner — different exposure.
Local is a modern color interior of a stone-walled altar with gold cross; Calisphere is a c.1900 exterior of a wooden steepled church — different photograph and likely different building.

Same Triangle Service Station, but local is a close view under the canopy at the pumps with two attendants ('Hood Tires' sign) while Calisphere is a wide street view of the arched station front with no people at the pumps.

Local postcard shows the long pediment-fronted Beaumont High School facade behind pepper-tree fronds; Calisphere shows the towered 'CITY HALL' building with POLICE arch and shrub mounds — facades do not visually match and it is certainly not the same exposure.

Only the WCTU fountain is shared: local shows it on the sidewalk beside the fluted-pilaster stone bank (1920s-30s); Calisphere is the 1910 dedication crowd in front of Gantt's General Merchandise — different era, location, and exposure.
Local is a class group portrait ('No. 13') of ~33 children against a wooden clapboard wall; Calisphere is a Mission-style masonry school exterior with no people — different photograph and building.

Both may include Laura Mae Stewart with an automobile, but local is the ribbon-decorated 'Beaumont Garage & Machine Co. Studebaker Six' parade car with five occupants while Calisphere is a ranch scene with Rez Stewart on horseback beside a touring car — clearly different exposures and events.
Local is the 1890s wooden bell-tower 'Beaumont School house' with picket fence and horse-drawn buggy; Calisphere is the later Mission-style masonry school — different building and photograph.
Identical mounted album print — same 'ENGINES AT BEAUMONT' typed label, same rounded-corner print, and every locomotive, track, and figure position matches exactly.
Local is the small gable 'Beaumont School 1890-1893' with tall pine; Cali 1910 shows a larger bell-tower building — different structure and exposure.
Both dirt-era Egan Ave, but local has the octagonal Beaumont Land & Water kiosk at right; Cali has false-front stores and a barn/warehouse with foreground ditch.
Local 1907 view shows horse teams and a 'Stables' false-front corner; Cali is the empty road/ditch view with warehouse — same street, different exposure.
Local is a street-level Frashers postcard of Sam's Cafe on Hwy 60/99; Cali is an elevated view of the Desert Outpost junction — different location and scene.
Identical hand-lettered 'FIFTH STREET'/'BEAUMONT-CALIF.' captions and identical car lineup (angled dark Ford at Al's Bakery, woodie wagon, right-side sedans).
Same instant: 'Century' trailer at the same spot on the highway, identical Chicken-Steak/Cabins/Dancing sign cluster, same parked cars and flatbed truck.
Local is a color interior of the stone chancel; Cali is an exterior postcard of the stone church — same building, entirely different photographs.
Local 1920s Triangle Service Station with gravity-feed pumps and two men in work clothes; Cali shows three bow-tied attendants at a later station with modern pump islands.
Same Mission-style BHS facade, but local is a distant corner view with overhanging pepper fronds and flagpole; Cali postcard is a close side-on view across striped roadway.
Local shows the pilastered granite elevation with the WCTU fountain on the sidewalk; Cali shows the ornate arched entrance with eucalyptus — same 5th/Egan bank corner, different exposure.
Local is a close class portrait ('No. 13') at a porch; Cali is a distant full-school assembly before the bell-tower building — clearly not the same exposure.
Local is a posed canopy-draped Studebaker Six float on a grassy roadside; Cali is the downtown parade procession with the Rexelo truck — possibly same festival but no shared exposure.
Local shows the cupola schoolhouse behind a new picket fence with horse and buggy and young trees; Cali 1910 shows mature trees and posed students — different exposure.
Same BHS gable-with-oculus building, but local (yearbook) has tall columnar cypresses/topiary balls and cumulus sky vs Cali's fuller conical trees and plain sky — different exposure.

Wide Frashers street postcard of 5th St vs close-up of an ornate bank entrance with tree and pedestrians; no shared exposure and the ornate espadana-parapet facade does not match the plain classical bank in the street view.

Both are Stewart Ranch horse-drawn harvest scenes, but local shows a long team pulling the combine rightward in dust, while Calisphere is a static straight-on loaded-harvester shot with horses on both sides, mounted on an album card.

Same Cherry Festival parade context, but local (McCulloh #220) shows girls marching past the Beaumont Woman's Club building, while Calisphere shows the Woman's Club truck float - entirely different moment and framing.
Local is Sam's Cafe on Hwy 60/99 in Beaumont (one-story street scene); Calisphere is the two-story Spanish-style Hotel Banning Cafe in Banning - different buildings and towns.
Local is a color 1950s photo of the Pass City Grocery storefront with parked cars; Calisphere is a b/w shot of flag-bearing horseback riders in the Stagecoach Days parade - no shared subject.

Local postcard shows the cobblestone Community Church with steep gable; Calisphere shows an earlier white wooden church with a tall steeple among eucalyptus - different structures, possibly the same congregation's earlier building.

Local is a standing portrait of Laura May Stewart with a horse's hindquarters at right; Calisphere shows her in a touring car with Rez Stewart on horseback beside a tank house - clearly separate exposures of the same family.
Local ('Laura in chaps 1911') shows her standing at a corral fence with lariat and windmill behind; Calisphere is the car-and-horseback scene - same person, entirely different photograph.

Same First Christian Church (matching crenellated corner tower, paired arched louvers, corner steps), but local is a 2017 color digital photo and Calisphere a vintage b/w print with cypress trees - decades-apart exposures.

Same 2nd Bank of Beaumont building, but local is a near-frontal shot of the side elevation with the WCTU fountain and a woman in a dark coat at the corner; Calisphere is an oblique corner view with a light-clad figure and Union Ice truck - different camera positions, not a crop.
Local is an oval CDV studio portrait of a bearded man (Reznor Stewart); Calisphere is the Stewart Ranch harvest field scene - portrait vs landscape, no shared subject in frame.

Identical crowd positions, identical 'Summit House' sign and Beaumont Land and Water banner, and the exact same diagonal torn-corner damage in the upper left - same photograph, evidently the same damaged print.

Local is a 1969 Daily Record-Gazette newspaper page with an architectural rendering plus a land-clearing photo; Calisphere is a photograph of the completed Maple Ave fire station with a fire engine - same station, not the same photograph.

Same Beaumont High School building (matching gabled pavilion with oculus window), but local shows bare newly built grounds and dirt road while the postcard shows mature cypress trees, hedge, and paved street - different eras and exposures.
Local is a 1930s B&W Frashers street scene with the 1920s stone bank; Calisphere is a 1960s color postcard of the mid-century First Western Bank building — different era, building, and scene.

Both show a Stewart Ranch horse-drawn harvester, but local is a side view of the rig in motion with a long horse team strung right; Calisphere is a posed frontal shot with crew standing on the machine.
Local is a parade of marching girls passing the Beaumont Woman's Club; Calisphere shows the Festival Queen and court posed in a cherry orchard with ladders — unrelated scenes.

Both show the Hwy 60-70-99 strip through Beaumont, but local centers Sam's Cafe corner with three parked cars; Calisphere is a down-the-centerline view of a different block with motel and gas-station signs — no shared structures identifiable.

Same Wellwood School campus, but local (newspaper halftone) shows the tile-roofed triple-arch arcade wing with fire hydrant; Calisphere shows the gable-end auditorium facade with oculus window from a different vantage.
Identical handwritten white 'Community Church' caption at top-left, same vegetation, sign board, and white curb post — same real-photo postcard exposure, local is just a higher-res scan.
Same three cars in identical positions, same tree and snow-capped ridge, identical shadows and awnings — same exposure with only minor crop/contrast differences.

Same First Christian Church, but local is an oblique view from the left showing the side elevation receding right; Calisphere is a near-frontal view with a hanging streetlamp at top-left absent from the local — different camera position/exposure.
Local is the 'S.P. Depot, Beaumont' platform postcard with crowd and tracks; Calisphere is a posed group beside 'Insectary Division' demonstration-train cars (Mar 17, 1909) — unrelated photographs.

Same Bank of Beaumont, but local is a near-square-on close view of the side elevation with the WCTU fountain prominent; Calisphere is a strongly oblique corner view — the perspective difference cannot come from cropping, despite a similarly dressed pedestrian in both.
Local is an oval carte-de-visite studio portrait of a bearded man (Reznor Stewart); Calisphere is a field photo of a horse-drawn harvester crew — completely unrelated images.

Identical diagonal missing/torn top-left corner, same 'Beaumont Land and Water Company' inscription, and identical crowd positions under the Summit House sign — same print, local slightly tighter crop.

Same Maple Ave fire station, but local is a 1969 newspaper page with an architect's line drawing plus a land-clearing photo (bulldozer, bare dirt); Calisphere is the completed 1971 station with trucks in bays.

Both depict Egan Ave, but local (c.1910s) shows the stone A.T. Ganty General Merchandise block with autos; Calisphere is an earlier dirt-road view with wooden false-front buildings and a foreground ditch — different era and exposure, no shared structures.
Local is c.1910 sepia photo of wooden post office with pergola and horse wagon; Calisphere image is a modern color postcard of a mid-century building with parking lot.
Local is a color interior of two men sorting cherries in crates; Calisphere is a B&W close-up of cherries on tree branches.
Identical marchers, crowd, and manure spots on road, plus the same McCulloh Studio '#220' mark in the corner of both prints.
Frame-identical school view including the same handwritten 'Beaumont Grammar School 1-5-11' caption at bottom.
Local halftone shows the 1921 Spanish-style stucco building with arched portico; Calisphere shows the earlier wooden schoolhouse with bell cupola and posed students — different building entirely.

Same office (same 'Easter Sunrise' poster and pigeonhole shelves), but local shows Bogart facing the camera with a long-haired cat on the desk; Calisphere shows him writing, shot from a different angle.

Cali is an elevated overview of the 5th/Egan block (San Gorgonio General Merchandise); local is a street-level view of the small Post Office building — same locale, entirely different vantage and exposure.
Identical crowd positions, 'Flowing Well Beaumont Cal.' lettering, and foreground shadows — same exposure.
Center-table crop matches exactly: same head poses, baby's tilt, napkin folds, and same blue ink mark on the bow-tied man's lapel; same 'Edinburgh Hotel' album mount.
Identical Lumber-Yard sign, fence pickets, tree canopies, and foreground culvert — same exposure.
Identical bare-tree branch structure, shadows, and framing of the Wellwood School facade — same exposure.

Identical horse stance (same white rear socks, front hoof position), rider pose, car occupants, and tank house behind — same exposure, local is a lower-res copy.
Local is the stone Bank of Beaumont building c.1940s with Union Ice truck; Cali is the c.1911 WCTU fountain dedication crowd — unrelated images.

Same stone Presbyterian/Community Church from a similar corner angle, but the 1968 newspaper view has mature street trees and a modern annex at left, while the postcard is an earlier closer view with ivy-covered walls.

Identical crowd and hillside 'FLOWING WELL EDGAR CANYON' lettering, including the same white damage spot at top center.
